notes: §1985:XVI.2.3.4 GR2: "Those segments having segment-numbers from the segment-limit through 49 are considered as overlayable fixed segments"; §1985:XVI.1.4.2 says such a segment, "if called for by the program, is always made available in its last used state". All-resident lowering gives exactly that: the ALTER target is an instance field (AlterSwitchEmitter.EmitFields/EmitAlter/EmitGoTo) that no segment change resets, and the clause is admitted at 85 by VisitSegmentLimitClause. The witness (limit 10, segment 20 PERFORMed twice) prints FIRST, LATER. Probes: r4a segment 20 re-entered after independent segment 60 overlaid it: S20 LATER; r4b limit 1 with segments 1 and 49 overlayable and 99 between: S1 LATER, S49 LATER; r4d limit 49 (only 49 overlayable): S49 LATER; class b and c as on 1985-GR-XVI.2.3.4-1 (r2i, r2c, r2f).
